summary: The ASSURE Act directs federal agencies to support increased access to voting by promoting voter registration, improving federal election websites, modernizing Vote.gov, and addressing voting access for specific groups like military personnel, federal employees, individuals in federal custody, and Native Americans.

affected_groups.effect: Must evaluate voter participation strategies, submit strategic plans, consider policies granting time off to vote and support poll-working, and potentially coordinate voter registration services.
Will receive annual opportunities to register, update info, or request absentee ballots, along with access to an end-to-end ballot tracking system.
affected_groups.group: Active-duty military personnel and overseas citizens

affected_groups.effect: Will receive educational materials on voting and voter registration assistance while in custody, notification of state-specific voting restrictions upon release, and support in obtaining valid state voter identification.
affected_groups.group: Individuals in federal custody and formerly incarcerated individuals

affected_groups.effect: Will be consulted by a federal steering group regarding voting rights, internet barriers, language access, and the use of Tribal identification cards for voting.
affected_groups.group: Native American communities and Tribal Nations

affected_groups.effect: Will be permitted to receive voter registration applications and general voting information from eligible non-partisan nonprofits at ceremonies.
affected_groups.group: New U.S. citizens at naturalization ceremonies

key_provisions: Directs federal agency heads to evaluate and implement ways to promote voter registration and participation, provide relevant information, and submit a strategic plan within 200 days.
Requires agencies to agree, to the greatest extent practicable, to designation as voter registration agencies if requested by a State under the National Voter Registration Act of 1993.
Mandates the modernization of Vote.gov by the General Services Administration, ensuring accessibility for individuals with disabilities and translation for language minority groups.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to establish annual procedures offering active-duty service members the opportunity to register to vote, update registration, or request absentee ballots, and to develop an end-to-end ballot tracking system.

Requires the Attorney General to establish procedures providing educational voting materials and facilitating voter registration for eligible individuals in Federal Bureau of Prisons custody and under supervision.
Establishes an Interagency Steering Group on Native American Voting Rights to consult with Tribal Nations and issue a public report on best practices for protecting Native American voting rights.

Directs U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to permit non-partisan nonprofit organizations to provide voter registration applications and information at administrative naturalization ceremonies.

Any penalties for agencies that fail to comply with strategic plan deadlines or designation requests.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The ASSURE Act directs federal agencies to support increased access to voting by promoting voter registration, improving federal election websites, modernizing Vote.gov, and addressing voting access for specific groups like military personnel, federal employees, individuals in federal custody, and Native Americans.
summary_detail.significance: The ASSURE Act directs substantial coordination across multiple executive branch agencies, the military, and federal correctional facilities to promote voter registration and facilitate voting access, though it relies heavily on agency evaluations, strategic plans, and voluntary state coordination rather than altering state election administration laws directly.
